item.name: Runner
item.effect: Increases player movement speed by 25%.
item.cardSummary: Runner is a pure overworld-mobility suit that makes your character move 25% faster, so traveling between areas and reaching battles is quicker. It does nothing in combat, so most players swap it out once they have a damage or capture suit.

item.name: Normal Novice
item.effect: Increases Normal-type skill damage by 5%.
item.cardSummary: Normal Novice adds 5% skill damage for Normal-type Evomon only, so it helps teams built around Normal attackers. Its narrow scope and small bonus make it an early-game filler until a wider damage suit drops.

item.name: Fire Novice
item.effect: Increases Fire-type skill damage by 5%.
item.cardSummary: Fire Novice gives 5% extra skill damage to Fire-type Evomon, making it a cheap pick for Fire-leaning teams. It only helps that one element, so its value depends entirely on how many Fire attackers you run.

item.name: Water Novice
item.effect: Increases Water-type skill damage by 5%.
item.cardSummary: Water Novice adds 5% skill damage to Water-type Evomon, a budget boost for Water-focused teams. Like the other Novice suits, it scales only with how much of your team shares that element.

item.name: Grass Novice
item.effect: Increases Grass-type skill damage by 5%.
item.cardSummary: Grass Novice raises Grass-type skill damage by 5%, helping teams that lean on Grass attackers. It is an early-game element suit you typically replace once a broader damage option appears.

item.name: Capture Experts
item.effect: Increases capture success rate by 5%.
item.cardSummary: Capture Experts improves your capture success rate by 5%, so wild Evomon are slightly easier to catch. It is an entry-level catching suit that the Epic Catch Master later outclasses.

item.name: Treasure Hunter
item.effect: Increases coins earned from battles by 15%.
item.cardSummary: Treasure Hunter adds 15% to the coins you earn from battles, speeding up everything coins buy, including more gacha spins. It is a strong farming suit when you are grinding currency rather than pushing combat power.

item.name: Breeder
item.effect: Increases Evomon EXP earned from battles by 10%.
item.cardSummary: Breeder grants 10% more Evomon EXP from battles, so your team levels faster while you grind. It is a leveling suit best worn during EXP farming rather than tough fights.

item.name: Catch Master
item.effect: Increases capture success rate by 10% and capture chance by 1.
item.cardSummary: Catch Master is the dedicated capture suit: +10% capture success and one extra capture attempt per encounter. It is the go-to choice when you are hunting and taming new Evomon.

item.name: Vanguard
item.effect: Increases first-turn damage by 22%.
item.cardSummary: Vanguard adds a large 22% bonus to damage on the first turn of a battle, rewarding fast, aggressive openers. It shines in short fights where you can win on the opening burst but does nothing after turn one.

item.name: Primal Mage
item.effect: Increases Fire, Water, and Grass skill damage by 5% each.
item.cardSummary: Primal Mage rolls the three elemental Novice bonuses into one suit, adding 5% skill damage to Fire, Water, and Grass attackers. It is a flexible damage option for mixed elemental teams that use the core three types.

item.name: Commander
item.effect: Increases one team slot's elemental skill damage by 8%.
item.cardSummary: Commander gives a focused +8% elemental skill damage to a single team-slot Evomon, so it rewards building around one strong elemental carry. Sources disagree on whether the slot is the lead or last Evomon, so confirm placement in-game before relying on it.

item.name: Physical Expert
item.effect: Increases Physical skill damage by 8%.
item.cardSummary: Physical Expert adds 8% damage to all Physical skills, regardless of element, making it a broad pick for Physical-attack teams. It pairs naturally with Evomon whose strongest moves are physical rather than special.

item.name: Special Expert
item.effect: Increases Special skill damage by 8%.
item.cardSummary: Special Expert mirrors Physical Expert for Special moves, granting 8% to all Special skill damage across elements. It is the better damage suit for teams that rely on special attackers.

item.name: Monster Hunter
item.effect: Increases Evomon EXP from battles by 10% and capture success rate by 15%.
item.cardSummary: Monster Hunter doubles as a leveling and catching suit: +10% battle EXP and +15% capture success in one slot. It is efficient for players who are both grinding levels and expanding their collection at the same time.

item.name: Elite Hunter
item.effect: Increases damage dealt to bosses by 11%.
item.cardSummary: Elite Hunter adds 11% damage specifically against bosses, making it a top pick for boss fights and raids. It does nothing against normal enemies, so it is a situational swap for tough encounters.

item.name: Guardian
item.effect: Reduces damage taken from bosses by 11%.
item.cardSummary: Guardian is Elite Hunter's defensive counterpart, cutting damage taken from bosses by 11% so your team survives longer in hard fights. It is most valuable on boss encounters where survival, not extra damage, is the bottleneck.

item.name: Elemental Mage
item.effect: Increases skill damage by 2% for each unique element in your party.
item.cardSummary: Elemental Mage scales with team variety, adding 2% skill damage for every unique element on your party, so a rainbow team gets the most out of it. It rewards diverse rosters and is weak on mono-element teams.

item.name: Mediator
item.effect: Allied Evomon take 8% less damage from the enemy lead Evomon's elemental type.
item.cardSummary: Mediator is a defensive suit that cuts 8% of the damage your team takes from the enemy lead's element, softening type-disadvantage matchups. Its value depends on the opposing lead's element, so it shines against predictable elemental threats.

item.name: Pharmacist
item.effect: Potions restore 20% more HP to allied Evomon.
item.cardSummary: Pharmacist boosts potion healing by 20%, stretching your healing items further in long fights and grinds. It is a sustain-focused suit that pairs well with potion-heavy playstyles rather than burst damage.

item.name: Energy Scholar
item.effect: Increases Ultimate skill damage by 16%, grants +1 initial Ultimate energy, and recovers 1 energy after each Ultimate used.
item.cardSummary: Energy Scholar is widely rated the best suit: it boosts Ultimate damage by 16%, starts you with extra Ultimate energy, and refunds energy after each Ultimate, so you use powerful Ultimates more often. It is the standout choice for Ultimate-driven teams.

item.name: Champion
item.effect: Increases all skill damage by 11%.
item.cardSummary: Champion adds a flat 11% to all skill damage with no conditions, so it helps every Evomon on any team. That universal, build-free bonus makes it one of the most beginner-friendly top-tier suits.
